lines.en: Hi, Tessa! Please sit down. **Tell me about yourself.**
lines.pt: Oi, Tessa! Por favor, sente-se. Fale um pouco sobre você.

lines.en: Thank you! I’m friendly, and I work in a bookstore.
lines.pt: Obrigada! Sou simpática e trabalho em uma livraria.

lines.en: Nice. What are you good at?
lines.pt: Legal. Em que você é boa?

lines.en: **I’m good at** talking to people. And I’m always on time.
lines.pt: Sou boa em conversar com pessoas. E sempre chego no horário.

lines.en: Do you have any work experience?
lines.pt: Você tem alguma experiência de trabalho?

lines.en: Yes. **I have experience in** customer service. Two years.
lines.pt: Tenho. Tenho experiência em atendimento ao cliente. Dois anos.

lines.en: Excellent. Do you have any questions for me?
lines.pt: Excelente. Você tem alguma pergunta para mim?

lines.en: Yes. What time does the shift start?
lines.pt: Tenho. A que horas começa o turno?

lines.en: At nine. We’ll call you this week.
lines.pt: Às nove. Vamos ligar para você esta semana.

pages.title: A simple job interview

situation.text: You have a short interview for a job in a store in the United States. You introduce yourself, say what you are good at and talk about your experience.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can introduce yourself in an interview, say what you are good at, talk about your experience and close the interview politely.
canDo: Introduce yourself: Tell me about yourself → I’m… I work…
Say your strengths: I’m good at…
Talk about experience: I have experience in…
Close politely: Thank you for your time.
success: I say one thing I am good at.
pages.think: How do you feel in a job interview? What helps you to stay calm?

extra: What job do you want?
What is your best quality?

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Interviews have their own habits in the United States. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: Being on time, or a few minutes early, shows respect.

cards.pt: Aperto de mão e contato visual
cards.note: A firm handshake and eye contact are common and show interest.
Many candidates send a short thank-you email after the interview.

qs.q: How do you greet the interviewer?

levels.A2: I say “Nice to meet you” and shake hands.
levels.B1: A smile, a handshake and “Nice to meet you” are a good start.
levels.B2: A brief handshake, eye contact and a warm greeting set a professional tone.

qs.q: What can you say about yourself?

levels.A2: My name, my job and one thing I am good at.
levels.B1: A short summary of your work, your skills and what you want.
levels.B2: A concise story: who you are, what experience you bring and why this job fits you.

qs.q: What do you do after the interview?
qs.pt: O que fazer depois da entrevista?

levels.A2: I say thank you and send a short email.
levels.B1: I send a thank-you email the same or the next day.
levels.B2: A brief thank-you email restates your interest and thanks them for their time.

pages.compare: In Brazil people also value being on time and a good first impression. Interviews may feel more formal or more personal. What is normal where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto: etiqueta de entrevista nos EUA.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: English gives strength to the important words (nouns, verbs, adjectives) and weakens small words. Strong words: GOOD, TALKing, PEOple.

items.say: I’m good at talking to people.
items.linked: I’m GOOD at TALK·ing to PEO·ple.

own.prompt: Write one sentence about what you are good at. Mark the strong words.
own.criteria: Say it twice, clapping on the strong words. Did the small words get weaker?

pages.title: Group mission — the interview
pages.goal: Each group must run a short job interview in English and decide who gets the job.

missions.mission: Interview for a café job. Ask about skills and experience.
missions.constraint: Use “Tell me about yourself” and “I’m good at…”
missions.start: Hi! Please sit down. Tell me…

missions.mission: The candidate has no experience. Show other skills and ask a question.
missions.constraint: Use “I can…” and “Do you have any questions for me?”
missions.start: Thank you for seeing me. I’m…

missions.mission: Two interviewers ask one question each. The candidate closes politely.
missions.constraint: Use “I have experience in…” and “Thank you for your time.”

success: Say what you are good at.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: conduzir e responder a uma entrevista curta.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão.
Progressão: com apoio → palavras-chave → sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
answers: Modelo: “Tell me about yourself.” → “I’m friendly, and I work in a bookstore.” → “I’m good at talking to people.”
extra: Who is the best candidate? Why?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short thank-you email after a job interview. Thank the interviewer and say you want the job.
pages.model: Hi Ian, **thank you for your time** today. I enjoyed learning about the job. **I’m good at** talking to people, and I would love to join your team. Best, Tessa
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos.
group: Troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one question about the job.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Language use

criteria.name: Pronunciation

criteria.name: Interaction

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Say a few words about yourself.

ladder.say: I’m friendly. I’m good at talking to people.
I have experience in customer service, and I’m good at solving problems.
Having spent two years in customer service, I’ve learned to stay calm under pressure.
What draws me to this role is the chance to apply my customer-service background to a team that values it.
ladder.goal: Link your goals to the job.

ladder.say: I would welcome the opportunity to contribute the depth of experience I have built, while continuing to learn.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
